Hello, everyone! I'm playing around with Nimble to see what I can get it to do. I'm trying to construct a relatively simple hierarchical regression model:
```
data=list(y = y, X = X, D = D, a = a, b = b)
inits <- list(beta = rep(0,p), tau = .5, phi = phi.mn)
m.nimble <- nimbleCode({

  ## Gaussian data model with mean=mu and Precision matrix = Prec.mat
  y[1:n] ~ dmnorm(mu[1:n], cov = Cov.mat[1:n,1:n])
  for (i in 1:n) {
    mu[i] <- X[i,] %*% beta[1:p]
  }

  ## defining the exponential covariance matrix
  for (i in 1:n) {
    for (j in 1:n) {
      Cov.mat[i, j] <- sigma.sq * exp(-D[i, j] / phi)
    }
  }

  ## Inverse-Gamma prior on sigma-squared
  sigma.sq <- 1 / tau
  tau ~ dgamma(0.01, 0.01)

  ## Gamma prior on phi
  phi ~ dgamma(a, b)

  ## Exchangeable vague Gaussian priors on each beta[i]
  for (i in 1:p) {
    beta[i] ~ dnorm(0, 0.000001)
  }
})
```
This model builds fine with
```
nimbleModel <- nimbleModel(m.nimble, data = data, constants = list(n=n,p=p), inits = inits)
```

However, when running
```
compiledModel <- compileNimble(nimbleModel)
```

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Compilation Error "[ is still there but nDim is not 0 (not a scalar)"
parts:
Hi Michael,
Thanks for posting and welcome to nimble.
nimble has strict types, including dimensionality, and this can be confusing.
I suspect the issue is that matrix multiplication always returns a matrix, but you are assigning X[i,] %*% beta[1:p] to a scalar.
Two ways to do this are (X[i,] %*% beta[1:p])[1,1] or (what I'd suggest) inprod(X[i,], beta[1:p]).
HTH
Perry
